the karyotype evolu- tion of pseudoscorpion species studied was characterized by a substantial decrease in chromosome numbers; the X0 sex chromosome sys- tem is widespread and probably an ancestral character in pseudoscorpion- es; and X chromosomes retain conservative meta- centric morphology in the majori- ty of species.

the karyotypes of geogary- pids and olpiids are characterised by a considerable reduction of the diploid chromosome number, the X0 sex chromosome sys- tem is widespread in pseudoscorpion taxa, the transient stage of diffuse chromatin condensation is recorded in pseudoscoprion males for the first time, and the relationships among some olpiid species are discussed based on the data of our research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first karyological data on pseudoscorpions belonging to the families Geogrypidae, Gary- pinidae and Olpiiidae.
the first karyological study of pseudoscorpion species of these families.
the first study of the karyotypes of geogarypid and olpiid pseudoscorpions, and the first record of diffuse stage in pseudoscorpion males.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pseudoscorpions studied have a X0 sex chromosomal system, a high degree of karyotypic stability and a low diploid chromosome numbers, but a high number of chromosomes per haploid set.
the karyotypes of geogarypid and olpiid species show considerable variation.
the karyotypes of geogarypid males are characterised by a high diploid number, the presence of a X0 system and the occurrence of a high number of bivalents at pachytene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the karyotypes of the studied species of pseudoscorpion taxa are characterised by a high degree of variation.
the chromosome number in pseudoscorpion species is variable, and the X0 sex chromosome is the most widespread in this group of arachnids.

the karyotypes of the studied pseudoscorpion species exhibit a great variation in the diploid number and in chromosome morphology, but the sex chromosome system and X chromosome morphology remain relatively constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pseudoscorpions are a very interesting and promising group for karyotype evolution studies.
the karyotypes of the families Geoga- rypidae, Garypinida and Olpiidae are characterised by a low diploid number and a high degree of karyotypic stabi- lity.
the karyotypic data of pseudoscorpion species can be useful for their systematics.
